standard.title: Similar topics in different texts
standard.description: identify how similar topics and information are presented in different types of texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students discuss different texts and identify features that indicate their purposes (AC9E1LY01). They have not yet compared how the same topic is presented across different text types — their prior work focused on identifying features within single texts, not across texts on the same topic.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify how similar topics and information are presented in different types of texts.

nodes.label: Same topic, different text types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that the same topic can be presented in different text types and name at least two text types that cover a given topic.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify two different text types that cover the same topic and name each type.
nodes.typical_width: Explore a topic across three or more text types — e.g. lifecycle in a poem, a narrative and an information report — and identify what each type is called and what its purpose is.
wider: Compare how a practical topic (e.g. recipes) is presented in print books, food packets, short video clips and digital apps — noting shared purpose and different forms
Identify a topic covered in a school subject and find multiple text types (textbook, website, picture book) that address it
success_criteria: Student can name at least two text types that present the same topic.
Student can identify the purpose of each text type they name.

nodes.label: What changes across text types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify at least one way the presentation of information differs across text types covering the same topic — e.g. organisation, language, detail level.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one difference in how the same information is presented in two different text types.
nodes.typical_width: Compare how a topic is presented across two or more text types — discussing differences in organisation, vocabulary, level of detail, use of images — and explain why each text type presents the topic in its distinctive way.
wider: Discuss what is learned from each text type about the same topic that cannot be learned from the others alone
Compare how a poem and an information report about the same topic use language differently and discuss why

response_modes.reason: Students often assume that one text type gives them all the information they need. Comparing multiple text types on the same topic — and noticing what each adds or emphasises differently — resolves the single-text misconception. More topic-and-text-type pairings is the productive investment.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Cross-text-type comparison of the same topic is a rich comprehension and critical literacy direction. Advancing students can explore what each text type enables and what it omits — genuine analytical depth within Year 2.
success_criteria: Student can name one difference between how the same information is presented in two different text types.
Student can explain one reason why the text types present the information differently.
